**Triage: lands in `packages/metadata-protocol` ⇒ `domain:metadata`; graded `pm:queue`, type `Bug`.** Restores a canonical pointer the platform already declares (ADR-0079) — accept set unchanged ⇒ `Bug`, not `Feature`, and nothing here is escalable.

## Premise verified on `origin/main` @ `84cb121`, not inherited

Both load-bearing claims hold verbatim:

```
packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:8603-8606
  const candidates = [
      obj.displayNameField,
      'name', 'full_name', 'title', 'subject', 'label', 'company',
  ].filter((c): c is string => typeof c === 'string' && hasField(c));

packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts:301   return { ...objectMeta, nameField: resolved };
packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts:314   return { ...objectMeta, fields, nameField: 'name' };
```

`provisionPrimary` does stamp `nameField` only. Zero-hit discipline satisfied — `displayNameField` returns **8** hits in that same file, so its absence from the two return statements is a real reading rather than a bad probe.

## ⚠️ One supporting claim in the card is measurably wrong — do not inherit it

> *"Three call sites in this file already spell exactly that … This would make the fourth, in the same function as the third."*

Measured: **one**, not three.

```
$ git grep -nE "nameField\s*\?\?" origin/main -- packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts
:7221:  displayField: gate.schema?.nameField ?? gate.schema?.displayNameField,
```

Counter-probe: `nameField` occurs only **5** times in the whole 16,480-line file, so the narrow match is real. The other two named symbols live in *other packages* — `assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable` in `packages/lint` and `packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts`, `expandSearchOnAst` in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` — and the third ("since #7643, `searchAll`'s own search-field resolution") **does not exist on `main` yet**, because #7643 is still `pm:dispatched`.

The defect itself is unaffected: the fix is still `obj.nameField ?? obj.displayNameField` as the first candidate, and the precedent for that spelling is still real — it is just cross-package precedent plus one local site, not a local pattern of three. The dev should not open the file expecting to find three.

## ⛔ Hard serial constraint — same function as an in-flight card

#7643 is `pm:dispatched` on **`searchAll`, the same function**, and this card's own scope note records that #7643 declared a region-limited file surface precisely because another PR was open on this file. This card must therefore either wait for #7643 to land or declare `renderTitle` at region level and hold to it. Do not dispatch this in the same batch as #7643.

Full picture for the file — four cards, regions listed on #8783. `domain:metadata` seat #6367 is **vacant**, so no seat currently holds this file's serial queue; flagged to the maintainer in this round's brief.

Impact bound is accepted as filed and is genuinely narrow: only objects whose primary title is outside `name` / `full_name` / `title` / `subject` / `label` / `company` fall through to `String(row.id)`. That narrowness is why it stayed invisible, and it is also why it grades `pm:queue` rather than a release nomination.

Concurrent region in this file: `auditMetaItem` `:6091` (#8747, in flight) — ~2,500 lines away. `diffMetaItem` `:15349` (#8671) has its PR open at #8797; no dev is editing the file. #8770 (#8421) is a **held** draft, parked.

## ⚠️ Triage's call-site count is now stale — I re-measured, and the news is good

Triage measured **one** `nameField ??` site and correctly flagged that the card's "three call sites in this file" claim was wrong. That measurement was taken at `84cb121` while #7643 was still `pm:dispatched`. **#7643 has since landed**, and it added exactly the site triage said "does not exist on `main` yet".

Re-measured on the current `origin/main` `f039a4ca`:

```
:7221   displayField: gate.schema?.nameField ?? gate.schema?.displayNameField
:8684   displayField: obj.nameField ?? obj.displayNameField        <- NEW, from #7643
:8640   obj.displayNameField,                                      <- the defect, unchanged
```

Counter-probe: `nameField` occurs **7** times in the whole file (was 5 pre-#7643), so the narrow match is real rather than a bad pattern.

**The operative fact: `searchAll` now contains both the correct spelling and the broken one, 44 lines apart, in the same function.** You are not importing a convention from another package — you are making `renderTitle` agree with the line 44 below it. Copy the spelling from `:8684`.

So: the card says "three sites, this would be the fourth" — wrong. Triage says "one site, cross-package precedent" — true when written, now stale. **Two sites, one of them in your own function.** Verify all three line numbers from the tree yourself; the file has moved twice tonight and will move again.

## The defect (premise verified by triage on `84cb121`, re-confirm on current main)

`renderTitle`'s candidate list reads `obj.displayNameField` — the **deprecated alias** — while `provisionPrimary`, the ADR-0079 designation seat the SchemaRegistry runs on every object at registration, stamps **`nameField` only**:

```
packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts:301   return { ...objectMeta, nameField: resolved };
packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts:314   return { ...objectMeta, fields, nameField: 'name' };
```

Triage's zero-hit discipline: `displayNameField` returns 8 hits in `display-name.ts`, so its absence from those two returns is a real reading.

Consequence: an object declaring `nameField` without the deprecated alias gets `undefined`, the entry is filtered out, and title falls through the conventional-name list to `return String(row.id)` — the palette shows a raw id where a declared, populated primary title exists.

## Scope — ⛔ presentation only

#7643 fixed **recall** (which rows come back) and deliberately left **titling** alone. This card is titling. Same function, different contract. ⛔ Do not touch search-field resolution, the object sweep, caps, ordering, or anything #7643 just landed — that code is hours old and its pins are load-bearing.

## Impact bound — accepted as filed, and it bounds your test too

Only objects whose primary title is **outside** `name` / `full_name` / `title` / `subject` / `label` / `company` are affected; everything else already resolves through the conventional list. That narrowness is why this stayed invisible, and it means your fixture must use a non-conventional title field or it will pass before and after.

## Verification bar

The card names the pin and it is a good one: an object declaring `nameField: 'company_name'` with **no** `displayNameField`, seeded with a populated `company_name`, must produce a hit whose `title` is that value rather than the record id. Add the discriminating control in the same test — an object using a conventional `name` still titles correctly — so the pin shows you changed precedence rather than bypassing the candidate list.

⚠️ **One judgement I want measured, not assumed:** if an object carries **both** `nameField` and `displayNameField` and they name different fields, your change flips which one wins. Measure whether any object in the repo is in that state before deciding it is safe, and pin the precedence you land on. If real objects disagree, ⛔ stop and report — that is a behaviour change beyond this card.

## ACCEPTED — PR #8809 marked ready and queued. All 26 gate jobs read job-by-job; zero failures.

PM session `session_01XeQRiAa7vYRVX5Fog7Zby8`, round 5.

### You resolved the one stop-condition by measurement, which is exactly what it was for

I made this a hard stop: *if an object carries **both** pointers naming **different** fields, your change flips which one wins — measure whether any object is in that state, and if real objects disagree, stop and report.*

You measured it rather than reasoning about it. Across 52 files carrying `displayNameField`, 38 declarations have a co-located `nameField`:

- **33 agree exactly**, each under an `[ADR-0079] canonical primary-title pointer (mirrors deprecated displayNameField)` comment;
- **5 disagree, and all five are test fixtures that exist precisely to pin precedence** — every one of them already pinning `nameField` as the winner, matching `resolveDisplayField({nameField:'a', displayNameField:'b'}) === 'a'` as pinned in `display-name.test.ts`.

So **no real object is in the disagreeing state**, and the precedence you landed on is the platform's existing answer rather than a new one. That is the difference between "the stop condition did not fire" and "I checked whether it fired" — and it is now pinned here too, so the next person does not have to re-derive it.

### The two controls that make the pin mean something

The pin alone (`nameField: 'company_name'`, no alias ⇒ title is `Acme Industrial`, not `acc_1`) would pass under a rewrite that short-circuits on the pointer and bypasses the candidate list entirely. Two of your six cases close that off:

- an object with a conventional `name` and **no pointer at all** still titles correctly;
- an **empty** pointer value falls through to the conventional entry — proving the pointer is a candidate in one ordered list, not a short-circuit return.

Using non-conventional title fields (`company_name`, `ref_no`, `ref_code`) throughout was necessary rather than incidental: a conventional field would have passed identically before and after the fix, and the test would have proved nothing.

Reverse verification: predicted before running, measured exactly **2 of 6 red**, with the defect's own signature (`expected 'acc_1' to be 'Acme Industrial'`, `expected 'OLD-11' to be 'TK-77'`). The 4 that stayed green are the controls, which by design do not discriminate this fix — worth saying, because a reverse verification where *everything* goes red is measuring the file, not the change.

### The line numbers held — and the corrected count was the operative one

You re-derived all four numbers from the tree before editing and they held exactly (`:8640` defect, `:8684` correct spelling, `:7221` gate, `:8552` `searchAll`), with `nameField` at 7 occurrences and exactly **2** `nameField ??` sites.

That count is the thing worth recording: the **card** claimed three local call sites (wrong), **triage** corrected it to one plus cross-package precedent (true when written, stale by dispatch — #7643 landed and added the second), and the truth was **two, one of them 44 lines below the defect in the same function**. Re-measuring at dispatch turned "import a convention from another package" into "make this line agree with the one below it", which is a materially easier and safer change.

### Scope held

Presentation only. #7643's recall contract untouched, its `protocol.search-case-fold.test.ts` pins still passing, search-field resolution / object sweep / caps / ordering unmodified. Region held to `renderTitle`, so the concurrent `auditMetaItem` and `diffMetaItem` work was unaffected — three cards in one 16,000-line file this round, no collisions.

### Noted, not actioned

`check:type-check-debt` reports `@objectstack/lint`'s TEST_DEBT records 20 while tsc measures 19 (**-1**) — a surplus another card's improvement opened. You left it, correctly: `--lower` in this PR would be an unrelated ledger edit. It is informational per the gate's own wording and tracked in #6376. **Three separate devs have now reported it tonight**, which is enough signal that it wants its own one-line card rather than a recurring footnote; I am carrying that rather than asking anyone to fold it in.

### Docs

Drift check flagged 3 pages; no action — this changes which declared field titles a search hit, and no page documents that resolution order.

### Landing

ready → auto-merge → merge queue. Confirmation on both readings — the timeline merge event **and** the artifact on `origin/main`.
